newsitem.title: FRANCE: Total signs technical support deal with Kuwait Oil.
newsitem.headline: Total signs technical support deal with Kuwait Oil.

text.p: French oil group Total SA said on Wednesday it had signed a three-and-a-half year agreement with the Kuwait Oil Company (KOC) to provide technical knowledge and support regarding KOC's upstream petroleum operations.
Under the agreement, Total will provide technical assistance in the management of operations related to exploration, production, transportation and export of crude oil.
The agreement was signed in Kuwait City by Khalid Al-Fulaij, chairman of KOC, and Total's Middle East president Christophe de Margerie.
The agreement became immediately effective. Total will provide consultancy using its technical know-how and expertise to help KOC develop its oil fields and maximising the benefits out of them.
Total said it hoped that the first cooperation with KOC would pave the way to the development of a mutually beneficial long-term partnership.
Charles Bowen is named general manager of Total in Kuwait.
A spokeswoman for Total said that the first applications of the KOC deal would concern the so-called "neutral zone" in the south of the country.
Media reports have said Total would be involved in developing the al-Wafta oil field, which is within the zone where both Kuwait and Saudi Arabia have claims on oil reserves.
The spokeswoman said the company hoped to be involved in more oil fields. She said Total was the third oil company to sign a similar deal with KOC after Chevron and British Petroleum Plc.
